orbit_cosmetic.physics.help: Axes as in Blockbench. Strength: pixels or degrees per block/second of movement (Turning: per quarter turn/second); negative reverses. Minimum and Maximum: how far it moves each way; a minimum of 0 keeps it from going the negative way (like a chest lid that must not sink in). Resistance: 0 reacts instantly, near 1 slowly and smoothly.

orbit_cosmetic.body_part.help: Every group of the file with something in it (HEAD, BODY, the arms and legs) replaces that part of the player, which moves it like the real one. A part can be up to 50% bigger than the player's own, and cannot be empty. Textures named PLAYER or SKIN (64x64, empty) show the wearer's skin. Body parts have no animations; the Particles tab adds particles.

orbit_cosmetic.particles.glow.tooltip: Drawn at full brightness, even in the dark
orbit_cosmetic.particles.spin.tooltip: How fast a particle turns on itself, in degrees per second. Each particle picks a speed between Spin min and Spin max; negative turns the other way.
orbit_cosmetic.particles.rotation.toolti: Each particle starts turned by a random angle, up to this far either way
orbit_cosmetic.particles.size.tooltip: A particle grows or shrinks from its start size to its end size over its life. 16 px is a block.
orbit_cosmetic.particles.offset.tooltip: Particles appear up to this far from the group either way, at random, in pixels (16 px is a block)
orbit_cosmetic.particles.help: Directions are relative to you when a particle appears, as in Blockbench: X to the side, Y up, Z to the back. Offset spreads where particles appear, at random. Speed is in blocks per second; Turn steers the particle like a car, in degrees per second. Changes are per second.
orbit_cosmetic.particles.look_help: Wait min and max are the time between two particles, in ticks (20 ticks is a second). Drag the player to turn it.
